**CSS custom properties — Beginner to Expert**

[Beginner]
Define reusable values with `--name` and read them with `var(--name)`.
```css
:root { --brand: #2563eb; --radius: 8px; }
.button { background: var(--brand); border-radius: var(--radius); }
```
Why it works: variables cascade and inherit, so every `.button` reads the root values.

[Intermediate]
Override variables per scope and use fallbacks in `var()`.
```css
.card--dark { --bg: #1f2937; --text: #f9fafb; }
.card { background: var(--bg, #fff); color: var(--text, #111); }
```
Why it works: the more specific scope replaces the value for its subtree only; fallbacks guard against typos.

[Advanced]
Compute with `calc()`, switch themes with one attribute, and animate registered properties.
```css
[data-theme='dark'] { --bg: #0f172a; --text: #e2e8f0; }
.panel { padding: calc(var(--space, 1rem) * 2); background: var(--bg); color: var(--text); }
```
Why it works: a single attribute on `<html>` re-themes the entire tree with no JS repaint loops.

[Expert]
Pass values from JS to CSS and build fluid type with `clamp()`.
```js
document.documentElement.style.setProperty('--accent', '#22c55e');
```
```css
h1 { font-size: clamp(1.5rem, 1rem + 3vw, 3rem); }
```
Why it works: one source of truth feeds both languages, and `clamp()` keeps sizing fluid between bounds.

**CSS box model — Beginner to Expert**

[Beginner]
Every element is a box: content, padding, border, margin, from inside out.
```css
.box { width: 200px; padding: 16px; border: 2px solid #333; margin: 8px; }
```
Why it works: width sizes the content area; padding, border and margin are added around it.

[Intermediate]
Set `box-sizing: border-box` globally so declared width includes padding and border.
```css
*, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box; }
```
Why it works: with `border-box`, `width: 200px` really renders 200px total, ending arithmetic surprises.

[Advanced]
Manage margin collapse: it happens between vertical margins of adjacent/parent-child blocks; prefer `gap` in flex/grid containers.
```css
.stack { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 1rem; }
```
Why it works: gap is real space on the container, so it never collapses with child margins.

[Expert]
Use logical properties (`margin-block`, `padding-inline`) and `inset` shorthand for direction-aware boxes.
```css
.notice { padding-block: .75rem; padding-inline: 1rem; margin-block-end: 1rem; }
```
Why it works: logical properties follow the writing direction, so RTL layouts need no overrides.

How should I organize the files of a static multi-page site?

Keep a predictable root: `index.html` plus one folder per concern, so any file's location is guessable.

```text
site/
  index.html
  about.html
  css/styles.css
  js/main.js
  img/
  fonts/
```

- HTML stays at the root so URLs stay clean (`/about.html`).
- Assets grouped by type (or by feature once the site grows) avoid duplicate names.
- Reference with relative paths and a single CSS/JS entry per page, so caching is simple:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="css/styles.css">
<script src="js/main.js" defer></script>
```

Why it works: one stylesheet and one deferred script per page maximize browser caching and keep the dependency graph flat.

Explain progressive enhancement for a static site with a small example.

Build the core experience in plain HTML first, then layer JS that upgrades — never replaces — it, so the page still works if JS fails.

```html
<form action="/search" method="get">
  <input name="q" type="search" placeholder="Search...">
  <button>Search</button>
</form>
```

```js
document.querySelector('form').addEventListener('submit', async (e) => {
  if (!window.fetch) return;               // old browser: native submit wins
  e.preventDefault();
  const res = await fetch('/search?q=' + encodeURIComponent(e.target.q.value));
  renderResults(await res.json());         // enhancement only
});
```

- Content and navigation must not depend on JS executing.
- Enhancement is feature-detected, not user-agent sniffed.

Why it works: the form submits natively without JS, and with JS users get the faster inline experience — one code path each, no dead ends.

What performance basics matter most for a static site: images, fonts, reflow?

Three highest-leverage moves: lazy responsive images, non-blocking fonts, and layout-stable animation. ```html ``` ```css @font-face { font-family: Main; src: url(fonts/main.woff2) format('woff2'); font-display: swap; } .animated { transition: transform .2s ease; } /* compositor-only */ ``` - `srcset`/`sizes` downloads only the bytes that match the viewport; width/height reserve space (no CLS). - `font-display: swap` renders text immediately; `preload` closes the gap for the one critical font. - Animate `transform`/`opacity` only — they skip layout and paint. Why it works: the browser fetches less, shows text sooner, and re-lays-out nothing during animation, which is exactly what LCP/CLS/INP measure.
